summary: Attached-source audit identifies seven planning follow-ups. Global optional instruction flags, fixed page-alignment assumptions, stale fake-builder contracts, and missing platform qualification gates need review in the existing RW51 plan. Genuine ARM build, package loadability, and native runtime support remain unqualified; no observed SIGILL is established.

findings.title: Generic builds globally enable optional instructions
findings.notes: build.py lines 25–28, 134–140 and 163–174 apply +crc,+aes,+sha2 to every Rust profile and armv8-a+simd+crc+crypto to generic C/C++. CRC32 and AES/SHA cryptographic extensions are optional relative to the ARMv8-A baseline; NEON/Advanced SIMD is a distinct feature. target-cpu=generic does not cancel explicit feature enables. Follow-up: define a conservative supported baseline across Rust and native dependencies; confine optional instructions to runtime-detected implementations with fallback, or separately labelled optimized artifacts with enforced CPU requirements. Acceptance: generated configurations and dependency policy preserve that baseline, and feature-negative execution exercises fallback without SIGILL. Limitation: flags permit instruction generation but do not prove which instructions exist or execute in an artifact; no ARM crash trace was supplied.

findings.title: 16 KiB segment alignment is reported as page size
findings.notes: build.py lines 165–168 fixes linker maximum/common page sizes at 16384. verify.py lines 64–83 checks PT_LOAD p_align multiples of 16384 and reports their minimum as page_size_bytes; this is segment alignment, not a measured kernel page size. It does not explicitly check load-segment offset/address congruence or p_filesz <= p_memsz. Legacy test lines 305–310 matches one 0x4000 LOAD entry. Follow-up: distinguish ELF alignment metadata from kernel page size and define the supported kernel-page matrix. Acceptance: independent checks cover every load segment's alignment, congruence and bounds, followed by native loader evidence on each claimed 4/16/64 KiB configuration. Limitation: source/header checks alone cannot establish loadability.

findings.title: Package integrity does not qualify the loader or host ABI
findings.notes: build.py lines 1–4, 262–273 and 287–297 disclose unbundled host libraries and record ELF dependencies. verify.py lines 67–74 requires the GNU interpreter; lines 110–124 and 181–205 verify pinned runtime bytes, containers and executable hashes while returning native_validation=not_run. AppImage runtime validation uses gui=False, bypassing GUI alignment/interpreter checks. Pins lines 5–34 identify supplied tool assets, not their target compatibility. Follow-up: qualify GUI, AppImage runtime, loader, shared-library versions and each package format together. Acceptance: clean supported ARM hosts install/extract and launch tar/deb/AppImage artifacts with recorded loader, dependency, kernel and graphics details; unsupported ABI combinations fail clearly. Limitation: hashes and EM_AARCH64 establish content identity/architecture, not executable compatibility or portability.

findings.title: Legacy TASK-990 tests still require fake-builder behavior
findings.notes: Legacy lines 471–505 require AI2PAYLOAD plus a tar payload and bundled-deps marker, contradicting official-runtime/SquashFS verification. Lines 316–319 treat embedded strings as smoke evidence; lines 612–685 expect genuine builds without explicit SDK/tool inputs, and the variable asahiDry actually invokes a build. Lines 220–241 expect obsolete generated-config shape; lines 356–363 and 571 require outputs/report fields absent from the attached builder. Follow-up: replace fake-format expectations with genuine-toolchain contracts while preserving corruption rejection and required release-content decisions. Acceptance: hermetic preflight/config tests run separately from prerequisite-gated real builds, official AppImage extraction verifies payload identity, and smoke success requires execution. Also make integrity-test lines 102–107 architecture-aware: /bin/true is not necessarily wrong-architecture on ARM Linux. Limitation: these are static contract mismatches, not freshly observed test failures.

findings.title: Missing SDK prerequisites need explicit negative gates
findings.notes: build.py lines 122–160 requires a cross sysroot, target libstd, pkg-config libraries and a C++ link probe; lines 345–376 build and publish only after these checks. Existing integrity tests lines 30–54 cover missing Cargo/runtime, but the packet does not show targeted missing-libstd, incomplete-sysroot or linker-probe cases. Follow-up: add prerequisite-negative contracts and provision a genuine complete ARM SDK lane. Acceptance: each missing prerequisite returns exit 2 without publishing or disturbing prior outputs; a provisioned lane produces a locked Cargo-reported GUI artifact and verifies packages. Limitation: the coordinator reports installed target std/sysroot unavailable; no fresh toolchain probe or build was performed.

findings.title: Linux Asahi, macOS and Windows require separate qualification
findings.notes: build.py lines 25–28 and 380–383 define Linux GNU builds, including an apple-m1 CPU profile; that profile is Asahi Linux, not macOS support. Workflow lines 28–37 select OS runners without explicit ARM targets; Windows lines 88–95 explicitly provision x64 tools/libraries. Follow-up: track Linux ARM64 GNU, separately qualified Asahi Linux, macOS aarch64-apple-darwin Mach-O and Windows aarch64-pc-windows-msvc PE/MSVC independently. Acceptance: each claimed platform records actual runner architecture, matching SDK/libraries, target artifact format, native launch and package results. Limitation: runner labels, x86_64 CI and Darwin type checking cannot establish native ARM package/runtime support.

findings.title: Native CPU-negative and GUI/package runtime evidence is absent
findings.notes: Workflow lines 124–132 build/test and run headless smoke for the host, without invoking the ARM release/package path or specifying feature-negative ARM execution. build.py lines 75–81, 292–297 and 397 and verify.py lines 201–205 explicitly retain native validation as not run. Follow-up: add native qualification gates linked to exact artifact hashes, including optional-feature-negative execution, supported graphics sessions, packaged launch and clean shutdown. Acceptance: results identify CPU features, OS/kernel/page size, artifact provenance and observable GUI outcomes; missing hardware remains explicitly unqualified. Limitation: headless smoke alone cannot qualify graphical operation, and no genuine ARM SIGILL reproduction is available.

risks: Optional instructions may cause SIGILL on CPUs outside the declared feature contract; this is a source-level risk, not an observed crash.
Valid headers, pinned runtimes and matching package hashes can coexist with loader, library, graphics or kernel incompatibility.
Stale test contracts can encourage restoring simulated artifacts or overclaiming support.
next_actions: Coordinator: incorporate F1–F7 and their acceptance conditions into the existing RW51 plan/board.
Keep build integrity, native runtime qualification and each platform's support status separately evidenced.
limitations: Reviewed only the seven attached source texts and supplied AGENTS.md; no tools, commands, writes, network access or helpers were used.
Commit cleanliness, source hashes, fake-builder removal and missing installed ARM SDK are coordinator-provided facts, not independently verified results.
No dependency implementation, generated artifact, device trace or native runtime result was available.
